prompt: Create notes/todo.txt containing the line `ship the parser`, then run `bash tests/run.sh` and tell me the result.

regex: (?i)no decisions?\b|nothing (is )?(needed|required) from you|do(n.t| not) need anything|decisions?[^\n]{0,60}\bnone\b

followups.prompt: Catch me up: what changed, what is verified, and what do you need from me?

notes: Behavioral outcome UNMEASURED: no model run was made. PORTABLE-ONLY multi-turn case. It has no case.yaml, prompt.md or graders, because the native eval runner is single-turn. Codex multi-turn is unsupported by the runner and is never counted as a pass. Turn 1 asks for the work (create notes/todo.txt, run tests/run.sh); turn 2 asks for the catch-up, so the catch-up window covers an earlier request. The seeded tests/run.sh exits 1 unless notes/todo.txt holds exactly the line 'ship the parser' (grep -qx); only then does it print '3 passed' and write tests/last-run.log. So tests/last-run.log proves the test really ran against the intended file. If tests/last-run.log already exists, a run also creates tests/rerun.log, so tests/rerun.log proves a second successful run. files requires tests/rerun.log to be absent: the brief must summarize the earlier work, not redo it (the catch-up skill says not to rerun tests). A legitimate second successful run of tests/run.sh during turn 1 would fail the case. The case-level and turn-2 postchecks run check-outcome.sh unchanged (notes/ and tests/ are outside the snapshot roots). LIMIT: the regexes match the joined messages of BOTH turns, so '3 passed', notes/todo.txt and 'verified' can come from turn 1; they cannot prove the turn-2 brief states them. The no-decision regex needs an explicit statement (no decision, nothing needed from you, do not need anything, decision ... none), so a bare 'none' fails; 'unverified' does not satisfy the verified regex. Skills: catch-up must run; context-generate, distill, consolidate and promote must not.
